comments: Looks good to me.  There are a good number of `Debug.Fail`/unreachable blocks that can be deleted with the `int`-returning-Span-writing variant.

review_comments:
Similarly, what does growth mean here?  That decrypt has returned an answer bigger than the key, which isn't possible (or, at least, you've stopped being RSA at that point).

It feels like we have "I expect the array, let's just allocate it first" and "I expect smaller than the array, let's rent it", and either way it's one and done.  No?
Do we really have a growth scenario here?  (Does this line stand a chance of being covered?)

In the real world, no. We should never get anything back bigger than the modulus (thus, key) size.

But, we depend on a virtual. Someone could be doing some "clever" (read: not clever) so I figured we can at least make it work. The happy-path works and we just allocate and return. For the unhappy path, it works. The happy path isn't penalized, the only penalty we are paying is a little bit of complexity.

If we want to just throw if the virtual gives us something back that is not "RSA", we can. It would certainly allow me to delete some tests.

Here's a test for the growth scenario:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5167e3498f36f844f661186456f459340153d6b8/src/libraries/System.Security.Cryptography/tests/RSATests.cs#L503
Ah, yes. And our base TryDecrypt just trusts the virtual, so this is being consistent.
